definitions.note: plural answer; the clue itself is one item of the plural

parts.note: to append is to add
the end is the final part
A is one of the musical notes

explanation.surface: An instruction to attach a closing comment, which is itself such a supplement.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points back at the clue: a note appended at the end is a single item of the plural answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Addenda are supplementary items appended to a book or document; a final note added is one such item.

clue.text: Quaint end of old cloth

parts.note: twee is British for affectedly quaint

indicators.note: the end of a word is its very last letter

parts.note: the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A charmingly old-fashioned remnant of aged fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: Twee is a British word for excessively dainty or cute.
explanation.definitionFit: Tweed is a rough woollen fabric, originally Scottish, used for jackets and suits.

clue.text: Unconscious after drink, having to leave society?

indicators.note: one piece placed after another comes second in the order

parts.note: a drop is a small drink
out cold means unconscious

explanation.surface: Someone passes out after drinking and must leave the club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after drink' suggests a drinking session, but it only orders the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To drop out is to withdraw from conventional society or from a course of study.

clue.text: Soldier to change sides twice

parts.note: to desert is to abandon one's side
a second word for changing sides: to rat is to betray

explanation.surface: A fighter who switches allegiance not once but two times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twice' asks for a second synonym of the same phrase. Desert Rats were the British 7th Armoured Division in North Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: A Desert Rat was a soldier of the British 7th Armoured Division in the North African campaign.
